verdict.rationale: GitHub's first-party authentication docs say you can generate an SSH key and add the public key to your GitHub.com account. That enables authentication for Git operations over SSH, which is exactly the story as written. Missing for 10: independent or hands-on corroboration, and documentation of key management details such as listing, removing, or auditing registered keys.

support.subject: As a developer, I can register SSH keys on my account to authenticate Git operations

citations.quote: you can add the public key to your account on GitHub.com to enable authentication for Git operations over SSH.
When you connect via SSH, you authenticate using a private key file on your local machine.
You can access and write data in repositories on GitHub using SSH (Secure Shell Protocol).
